option.label: Knotty base (firmness not specified)
option.detail: Gould describes often knotty bases. A knotty crown does not establish a rhizome or by itself measure hardness.

option.label: Rhizomes not developed
option.detail: Gould explicitly describes no developed rhizomes in this treatment. Inspect the base; a knotty crown is not by itself an underground runner. Other accounts report short rhizomes, so preserve that source disagreement.

option.label: Sheath stiff hairs arise from raised bases
option.detail: Look on the sheath, not the blade or node, for stiff hairs on small raised papilla-like bases. Gould also permits hairless sheaths.

option.label: Spikelets on short individual stalks
option.detail: Follow the small pedicel of one spikelet on a spreading panicle branch. This is not a sessile-plus-pedicelled spikelet pair.

option.label: Spreading panicle branches rebranch freely
option.detail: Check the whole branching architecture: primary branches spread and branch again. Do not infer fixed branch counts or clustered spikelets.

option.label: Lower glume present and shorter than spikelet
option.detail: Find the first outer scale. Gould gives 1–1.5 mm for a 2.8–3.2-mm spikelet; it is present and shorter, not an absent glume.

option.label: Lower glume broad at base, abruptly pointed
option.detail: Follow the lower glume from its broad base to its abruptly narrowed acute apex. Do not confuse it with the smooth shiny upper floret lemma.

option.label: Second glume and lower lemma about equal
option.detail: Compare the second outer glume with the LOWER lemma inside it. The lower lemma belongs to the male floret, not the upper fertile floret.

option.label: Second glume longer than lower lemma
option.detail: This is an alternative Gould permits to the two scales being about equal. Do not transfer this length comparison to the first glume or upper fertile lemma.

option.label: Lower floret male (staminate)
option.detail: Open one spikelet to locate the lower floret and its male organs. A male floret is not an empty sterile scale or a separate stalked spikelet.

option.label: Lower floret palea broad, thin, as long as upper floret
option.detail: Identify the palea of the lower male floret. Gould describes it as broad and thin, matching the upper floret in length; this is not the upper lemma surface.

option.label: UPPER floret lemma smooth and shiny
option.detail: Inspect the lemma enclosing the upper floret. Do not transfer the lower floret's thin palea texture to this lemma; smooth/shiny alone does not add an unreported hardness claim.

option_additions.subgroup: Upper floret lemma surface and apex

option.label: UPPER lemma has a slight apical beak
option.detail: Inspect the apex of the upper floret lemma. A slight beak is not automatically an awn or a proven midvein mucro.

option_additions.subgroup: Upper floret lemma surface and apex

option.label: Whole spikelet without hairs
option.detail: Examine the mature spikelet itself. Hairless spikelets can coexist with hairy sheaths, nodes or blades on the same plant.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: A knotty tufted base is not proof of a rhizome
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould describes tufted culms, often with knotty bases, and explicitly says rhizomes are not developed. Older H&L and species notes report short knotty rhizomes. Keep this disagreement visible: a rhizome observation remains possible but unresolved, not a fully documented Kleingrass match.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: The switchgrass treatment starts separately below the distribution/flowering continuation and explicitly describes scaly creeping rhizomes. Do not transfer those roots to Kleingrass.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Preferred exact Gould account versus preserved regional/supplemental disagreement; no local voucher or overseas-variety determination.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Measure the true fringed membrane and separate vegetative hairs
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: The true membranous ligule is 0.5–2 mm INCLUDING hairs. Nodes may be hairless or minutely hairy; sheaths hairless or stiff-hairy with papilla bases; blades hairless or stiff-hairy on one or both faces. Blades mostly 2–6 mm wide, occasionally 8 mm.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Outside sheath hairs do not establish a hair-only ligule. Nearby switchgrass dimensions and hair patterns are not this treatment.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact named-species source; variant states are alternatives, not mandatory simultaneous features.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Open one spikelet and identify first glume, lower male floret and upper lemma
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Hairless spikelets mostly 2.8–3.2 mm stand on short pedicels on spreading rebranched panicle branches. The first glume is present, 1–1.5 mm, broad-based and abruptly acute. Compare the second glume with the lower lemma; they are about equal or the second glume is longer. The lower floret is male, with a broad thin palea as long as the upper floret. The upper lemma is smooth, shiny and slightly beaked.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Do not treat the lower palea as the upper lemma, the apical beak as a proven awn, or the first glume as missing. A Panicum obtusum illustration caption on p.453 belongs to another species.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact organ-level description from pp.452–453; photographs and local plant identity not re-certified.

preferred_field_rule: Gould's Kleingrass (Panicum coloratum L.) is a tufted perennial, often knotty at the base, with NO DEVELOPED RHIZOMES in this account. H&L/older notes report short rhizomes: those routes remain possible but unresolved, never proven from a knotty crown. Look for an open freely rebranched panicle, hairless 2.8–3.2-mm spikelets on short pedicels, a present 1–1.5-mm first glume, lower male floret with broad thin palea, and smooth shiny slightly beaked upper lemma. The 0.5–2-mm ligule includes its fringe hairs. Existing mat/rooted-surface-stem accounts remain separately conditional; Gould does not address stolon absence here. Existing Australian var. makarikariense reference photographs do not establish a local Texas variety or specimen identity.

non_scoring_context.distribution: Introduced forage in southern/central Texas and persisting on Edwards Plateau (region 7); native Africa, introduced broadly in warmer regions. Historical source account, not a county voucher.
non_scoring_context.flowering: Mostly May–September in Gould; not current local phenology certification.

adjacent_material_excluded: Panicum obtusum Fig.241 caption is not a Kleingrass illustration.
Panicum virgatum treatment begins after Kleingrass distribution/flowering: its rhizomes, dimensions and chromosomes are separate.
Not P. coloratum Walt. or P. coloratum Cav.
omissions_not_absences: Gould does not specify a leaf tip, edge, midrib/venation or auricle state here.
No sheath opening or stolon presence/absence is stated.
No explicit culm growth angle, node glands or callus/rachilla hairs are stated.
The slight upper-lemma beak is not a confirmed awn or mucro.
